searchText: Hey guys, I am currently reading the HF1 spec and there are a few things I don't understand. I hope it's OK if I dump some questions here. Today I would like to enquire about `process_attestation`. 1. It doesn't make sense to have both `assert is_matching_source` and `if is_matching_source`, although I am not sure which one can be removed. 2. Why do we check `if is_matching_head and is_matching_target` and not just `if is_matching_head`? 3. Why do we have `+ integer_squareroot(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)` when verifying timely source and `+ SLOTS_PER_EPOCH` when verifying timely target? Why not have the same value for both? I'm curious, why do we need a separate shuffling for sync committees, and would it be feasible to create a correlated shuffling, for example by running one extra round on the other committees? shuffling indices is currently the major bottleneck in the eth2 state transition - adding one more adds to the burden - the problem also grows worse with the validator set size, because more memory needs to be touched > 1. It doesn't make sense to have both assert is_matching_source and if is_matching_source, although I am not sure which one can be removed. the `assert` ensures that attestations are consistent w/ the current view of the chain, namely the current justified checkpoint actually seems like we can drop the conditional looking... in that case the `if is_matching_source` check later on can be removed right because it will always be `true` care to make a PR? 🙂 ` if is_matching_source and state.s...` was included for symmetry with the other conditionals there even though it was pre-validated in an above assert I don't feel terribly strongly about it, but Justin might 😅 (2) because we don't want a scenario where you can get reward for head but no contribute to FFG finality (getting target correct) yes, the head implies the target, but we don't check consistency for inclusion on chain Note, this condition for reward is in phase 0 because `get_matching_head_attestations` calls `get_matching_target_attestations` we could define `is_matching_head` as `data.beacon_block_root == get_block_root_at_slot(state, data.slot) and is_matching_target` maybe that is a bit clearer? all of them have an implicit `is_matching_source` because of the assertion... > 3. Why do we have + integer_squareroot(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH) when verifying timely source and + SLOTS_PER_EPOCH when verifying timely target? Why not have the same value for both? this is basically an extra incentive to get the attestation on-chain quickly in sqrt(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH), rather than just w/in SLOTS_PER_EPOCH the high-level answer is security -- this shuffling is "firewalled"from the other shuffling(s) which keeps it semantically clean, a big concrete difference is that this shuffling only changes once per day, rather than every epoch trying to think what happens if we did the "correlated shuffling" like you suggest Like, just using the first 1024 validators in the beacon shuffling as the sync committee? hmm I know I did not think about it explicitly; I just have a cryptographer's "domain-separate everything by default" instinct I suppose it could be done that way Currently sync committee allows for duplicate indices though. It's very unlikely we'll reach that case but still Well, the issue came up when optimising the proposer vs committee shuffling really in the state transition - this adds one more, and there are more to come - it's something worth considering that's also doable with the beacon shuffling approach Just so `get_shuffled_index(i % committee_length)` Sure, I mean "security" is fine, but also.. Imprecise 😀 And I agree, once per day isn't that bad except.. Its a cumulative effect, and at some point its good to ask the question at least Ah right, the fact that the shuffling is once per day means that in 255 of 256 epochs it will be mismatched with any other shuffling anyway

excerpts.content:
Hey guys, I am currently reading the HF1 spec and there are a few things I don't understand. I hope it's OK if I dump some questions here. Today I would like to enquire about `process_attestation`.

1. It doesn't make sense to have both `assert is_matching_source` and `if is_matching_source`, although I am not sure which one can be removed.
2. Why do we check `if is_matching_head and is_matching_target` and not just `if is_matching_head`?
3. Why do we have `+ integer_squareroot(SLOTS_PER_EPOCH)` when verifying timely source and `+ SLOTS_PER_EPOCH` when verifying timely target? Why not have the same value for both?

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: I'm curious, why do we need a separate shuffling for sync committees, and would it be feasible to create a correlated shuffling, for example by running one extra round on the other committees? shuffling indices is currently the major bottleneck in the eth2 state transition - adding one more adds to the burden - the problem also grows worse with the validator set size, because more memory needs to be touched

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: > 1. It doesn't make sense to have both assert is_matching_source and if is_matching_source, although I am not sure which one can be removed.

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: the `assert` ensures that attestations are consistent w/ the current view of the chain, namely the current justified checkpoint

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: actually seems like we can drop the conditional

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: looking...

excerpts.author: radekkapka
excerpts.content: in that case the `if is_matching_source` check later on can be removed

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: right

excerpts.author: radekkapka
excerpts.content: because it will always be `true`

excerpts.author: ralexstokes
excerpts.content: care to make a PR? 🙂

excerpts.author: djrtwo

this is basically an extra incentive to get the attestation on-chain quickly
